chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: What the original Ink Spots sang
summary: They did harmony songs like Beautiful Doll, International Rag, Somebody Loves Me and Mother, and he wishes he had written them a defining song.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: famous by the name of the Ink Spots. Deek Watts was from Indianapolis and I don't know where the other boys were from. But they had Deek Watson, they had Bill Kenny and two other boys from time to time, they'd take one out and put one in. However, they made a big name out of the Ink Spots, you know. But we started it. Buck and Bubbles started that and we were the first three Ink Spots and that was about the year of 1914 -'15 -- '14 I think it was, 1914, something like that. It could have been a little later. But it seems like those were the years.
When you first established the Ink Spots what kind of things did you do together?

Harmony singing. We sang songs like "International Rag," "Beautiful Doll," I know you've heard that number before -- "Oh, you beautiful doll, You great big beautiful doll Let me put my arms around you I could never do without you Oh, you beautiful doll, You great big beautiful doll

I 'scared to leave you
'Cause my heart would break
I don't want you to break
'Cause you can't (inaudible)
Oh, oh, oh, you beautiful doll."

Then we sang another song
called -- oh, Lord, I can't remember all the
songs, it was so far back, goes way back, that's
over 50 years back. It's hard for me to
remember the songs we sang.

This is where I got to the
place where I just sit down and start to,
you know, meditating over things I've done,
then I can go into what the songs were.

Then we did "Somebody Loves
Me," and we did -- only thing at that time my
mind wasn't creative and I didn't create a song
for the Ink Spots. I would have written a song
for the Ink Spots, if you understand what I'm
trying to say. There should have been a song
of the Ink Spots, who we were, like a definition
of the word Ink Spots, you know. "I" is for
this and "n" is for that. I'm going to do my

name that way, a definition of John Bubbles.
I was thinking of a song called "Mother,"
remember "Mother?"

"Thank you for the million things
you gave me
All because of that she's growing
old
T for the tears she shed to save
me
"H" is for the heart that's pure as
gold
"E" is for her eyes with love light
shining
"R" means right is right she'll always
be
Put them all together they spell
Mother
A word that means a world to me."

That was a beautiful song.
And we sang the "Dark Town
Strutters Ball"

"I'll be down to get you in a taxi
honey
You better be ready 'bout half-past
eight
Now darlin' don't be late
I want to be there when the band starts
playin'
Remember when we get there, honey
Two steps we're going to have them all
We'll wear out both our shoes
When they play those jellyroll blues
Tomorrow night at the Dark Town
Strutters Ball."
